mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% triggers a risk premium adjustment that drives positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% in the current month
failure_condition: Over the 20-day horizon, SPX 20d returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) when CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in PAYEMS labor cost index exceeding 0.5% is associated with higher wage growth expectations, which elevates S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by more than 0.5% in the current month
failure_condition: In regimes where PAYEMS rises >0.5%, the 60-day SPX forward returns are negative on average (mean < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly expansion in INDPRO supply index above 95 suggests robust manufacturing activity, which predicts negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns due to over-supply risk.
failure_condition: Over multiple non-overlapping 5-day windows, INDPRO >95 is associated with non-negative SPX 5d returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both HOUST and RSAFS retail sales (monthly) signals weakening demand, which is expected to produce negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: When both HOUST and RSAFS decline month-over-month, 20d SPX returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in FEDFUNDS below 2% for three consecutive months indicates persistent monetary easing, which should drive positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls below 2% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 60 days following the trigger, SPX 60d returns are not statistically higher than the prior 60-day mean (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected rise in UNRATE above 5% in a month signals tighter labor market expectations, which should produce negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by more than 0.5 percentage points in the current month
regime_hint: sudden tightening in labor market expectations
failure_condition: When UNRATE jumps >0.5pp, the 20d SPX returns are not significantly negative (mean >= 0, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in GDPC1 demand index (quarterly) below 100 suggests an economic slowdown, which should be associated with negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls below 100 in the most recent quarter
failure_condition: After GDPC1 <100, 20d SPX returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) in 70% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in PAYEMS and GDPC1 indicate weakening consumer and business demand, which should drive negative S&P 60-day forward returns when both signals persist for two months.
candidate_trigger: both PAYEMS and GDPC1 decline for two consecutive months
failure_condition: When the two-month decline in both proxies occurs, the 60-day SPX returns are not significantly negative (mean > -0.01, p > 0.05).
